headline: Black Friday bounce trims a rocky month, Fed still the wildcard
body: Wall Street closed out a turbulent November with a relief rally: Friday's shortened post-Thanksgiving session saw the Dow add well over 1%, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both following higher, after a mid-week stretch that showed just how jumpy positioning had become — the S&P swung roughly 3% and the Nasdaq nearly 5% intraday on Wednesday before dip-buyers stepped back in. Even with the bounce, the month's scoreboard reads defensively: the Nasdaq is on track to snap a seven-month winning streak and sits down a couple percent for November, while the S&P and Dow are closer to flat, both having clawed back from sharper tech-driven drawdowns earlier in the month tied to doubts about AI infrastructure spending paying off on the timeline investors had assumed.

The swing factor remains Fed policy under chair Kevin Warsh, whose recent commentary has leaned hawkish enough that futures markets are leaning toward a December rate hike rather than the cuts investors were positioned for earlier this year — a reversal that has made the market's most richly valued AI-linked names the most volatile. With the long weekend thinning out volume and headlines, there isn't much fresh retail-chatter signal to point to today; this read leans on the holiday-week price action and the rate-hike narrative rather than social-media positioning, which was notably quiet over the break.
